subject: maths
title: Maps and Directions: Position Words, Paths and Bird’s-Eye Views
seo_title: Year 2 Maps and Directions Worksheets: Position Words and Paths (Free)
standard_text: Locate positions in two-dimensional representations of a familiar space; move positions by following directions and pathways
meta_desc: Free Year 2 maths worksheets on maps and directions: position words on a classroom map, follow directions like forward 3 and turn left, paths on a grid, which path is shorter and bird’s-eye views. 100 questions with an answer key, Australian Curriculum aligned.
key_big: Count the squares you move, not the square you start on.
key_sub: Left and right on a map are the left and right of the page. When a person faces another way, use their left and right: turn the map to check.
body_html:
What a map is

A map shows a place from above, like a bird flying over it. This is called a bird’s-eye view. Each shape on the map stands for a real thing.

Where is it?

Use position words: next to, between, left of, right of, above, below. On a map, above means towards the top of the page and below means towards the bottom.

Example

What is just below the fish tank?

Find the fish tank. Look one square down.

Answer: the reading mat

Follow a path

Count the squares you move. Do not count the square you start on. Do one step at a time.

Turn left and turn right

A robot or a person turns to their own left or right. If they face the bottom of the page, their left is on the right of the page. Turn the page around to check.

Which path is shorter?

Count the squares along each path. The path with fewer squares is shorter. A path with more turns is not always longer.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the start squareCount the moves, not the square you stand on
Using the page’s left and right for a person who faces youTurn the map so you face the same way as the person
Going the wrong way (down instead of up, left instead of right)Up is the top of the page. Check with your hands before you move.
Choosing the path that looks shorterCount the squares on each path, then compare
Choosing the side view for a bird’s-eye viewImagine looking straight down from above

faq.q: What do Year 2 students learn about maps in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: In Year 2 (AC9M2SP02) students find places on simple maps of familiar spaces, like the classroom or playground, and follow directions and paths such as “forward 3, turn left”.

faq.q: How can I help my child tell left from right?
faq.a: Hold up both hands with the fingers up and thumbs out: the left hand makes an L. Practise with games like “turn left at the letterbox” on a walk.

faq.q: Why do children mix up left and right on a map?
faq.a: When a person on the map faces the bottom of the page, their left is on the reader’s right. Turning the map or standing the same way as the person fixes this.

faq.q: Do Year 2 students use north, south, east and west?
faq.a: Year 2 mostly uses left, right, forward, back and turns. Compass points like north and south come in the later years.

sets.title: Position words on a classroom map: next to, between, left, right, above and below

items.q: How many things are in the bottom row of the map?
items.e: Look along the bottom row: the door, the bag hooks, the laptops and the plants. That is 4 things. One square is empty.

items.q: What is between the lockers and the plants?
items.e: Find the lockers and the plants. They are in the same column. The bins are in the middle of them.

items.q: What is just to the right of the books?
items.e: Start at the books. Look one square right. That square is the whiteboard.

items.q: What is in the top left corner of the map?
items.e: Top is the top row. Left is the left side. The books are in the top left corner. The sink is in the top right.

items.q: Which is next to the plants?
items.e: Next to means touching, side by side. The bins are just above the plants. The square on the left of the plants is empty.

items.q: What is just below the fish tank?
items.e: Start at the fish tank. Look one square down. That square is the reading mat. The books are on the other side.

items.q: What is just above the teacher’s desk?
items.e: Start at the teacher’s desk. Look one square up. That square is the whiteboard.

items.q: What is between the whiteboard and the sink?
items.e: Find the whiteboard and the sink. They are in the same row. The window is in the middle of them.

items.q: What is in the bottom right corner of the map?
items.e: Bottom is the bottom row. Right is the right side. The plants are in the bottom right corner.

items.q: What is just to the left of the sink?
items.e: Start at the sink. Look one square left. That square is the window.

items.q: What is between the books and the reading mat?
items.e: Find the books and the reading mat. They are in the same column. The fish tank is in the middle of them.

items.q: What is just to the right of the door?
items.e: Start at the door. Look one square right. That square is the bag hooks.

items.q: Which of these is not on the map?
items.e: Read every label on the map. There is a fish tank, a sink and laptops, but no piano.

items.q: What is just below the sink?
items.e: Start at the sink. Look one square down. That square is the lockers.

items.q: What is just to the left of the laptops?
items.e: Start at the laptops. Look one square left. That square is the bag hooks.

items.q: What is between the door and the laptops?
items.e: Find the door and the laptops. They are in the same row. The bag hooks are in the middle of them.

items.q: What is just above the door?
items.e: Start at the door. Look one square up. That square is the reading mat.

items.q: What is just to the left of the bag hooks?
items.e: Start at the bag hooks. Look one square left. That square is the door. The laptops are on the other side.

items.q: What is just above the lockers?
items.e: Start at the lockers. Look one square up. That square is the sink. The bins are on the other side.

items.q: What is between the sink and the bins?
items.e: Find the sink and the bins. They are in the same column. The lockers are in the middle of them.

sets.title: Follow directions: forward, back, turn left and turn right

items.q: The robot faces the bottom of the page. It goes forward 3. Where does it stop?
items.e: Move 3 squares down the page, one square at a time. Do not count the square the robot starts on. It stops on A.

items.q: The robot faces the top of the page. It goes forward 2, turn right, forward 3. Where does it stop?
items.e: First go forward 2. Then turn right: now the robot faces right. Then go forward 3. It stops on A.

items.q: The robot faces the bottom of the page. Which steps take it to the star?
items.e: Go down 2 squares. The robot faces the bottom of the page, so turning right makes it face the left of the page. Then go 3 squares.

items.q: The robot faces right. It goes forward 3. Where does it stop?
items.e: Move 3 squares right, one square at a time. Do not count the square the robot starts on. It stops on B.

items.q: The robot faces right. It goes back 2. Where does it stop?
items.e: Back means the robot moves the opposite way to where it faces. It does not turn. Move 2 squares to the left. It stops on B.

items.q: The robot faces right. It goes forward 2, turn left, forward 2. Where does it stop?
items.e: First go forward 2. Then turn left: now the robot faces up the page. Then go forward 2. It stops on D.

items.q: The robot faces left. It goes forward 2. Where does it stop?
items.e: Move 2 squares left, one square at a time. Do not count the square the robot starts on. It stops on C.

items.q: The robot faces the top of the page. It goes back 2. Where does it stop?
items.e: Back means the robot moves the opposite way to where it faces. It does not turn. Move 2 squares down the page. It stops on B.

items.q: The robot faces the bottom of the page. What must it do to face the star?
items.e: The robot faces the bottom of the page, so its left is on the right of the page. It turns left to face the star.

items.q: The robot faces right. What must it do to face the star?
items.e: The star is behind the robot. A half turn makes it face the other way.

items.q: The robot faces the top of the page. It goes forward 3. Where does it stop?
items.e: Move 3 squares up the page, one square at a time. Do not count the square the robot starts on. It stops on D.

items.q: The robot faces the top of the page. It goes forward 3, turn left, forward 2. Where does it stop?
items.e: First go forward 3. Then turn left: now the robot faces left. Then go forward 2. It stops on C.

items.q: The robot faces the bottom of the page. It goes forward 2, turn left, forward 2. Where does it stop?
items.e: The robot faces the bottom of the page, so its left is on the right of the page. Turn the page upside down to check. Go forward 2, turn left (now it faces right), then go forward 2. It stops on D.

items.q: The robot faces left. How many squares must it go forward to reach the star?
items.e: Count the moves, not the robot’s own square. Forward 3 takes the robot to the star.

items.q: The robot faces the top of the page. Which steps take it to the star?
items.e: Go up 2 squares. Turn right, so the robot faces right. Then go 4 squares to the star.

items.q: The robot faces the bottom of the page. It goes forward 3, turn right, forward 1. Where does it stop?
items.e: The robot faces the bottom of the page, so its right is on the left of the page. Turn the page upside down to check. Go forward 3, turn right (now it faces left), then go forward 1. It stops on A.

items.q: The robot faces the top of the page. What must it do to face the star?
items.e: The robot faces the top of the page. The star is on its right side, so it turns right.

items.q: The robot faces right. How many squares must it go forward to reach the star?
items.e: Count the moves, not the robot’s own square. Forward 4 takes the robot to the star.

items.q: The robot faces right. It goes forward 3, turn right, forward 2. Where does it stop?
items.e: First go forward 3. Then turn right: now the robot faces down the page. Then go forward 2. It stops on B.

items.q: The robot faces left. It goes forward 2, turn right, forward 2. Where does it stop?
items.e: The robot faces left. Its right hand points up the page. Go forward 2, turn right (now it faces up the page), then go forward 2. It stops on C.

sets.title: Paths on a grid map of the playground

items.q: Which steps take you from the toilets to the bike racks?
items.e: From the toilets, count the squares across, then the squares up or down: 2 squares right, then 4 squares down. Count the moves, not the square you start on.

items.q: Start at the bench. Go 3 squares right. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the bench. Go 3 squares right. You reach the garden. Do not count the square you start on.

items.q: How many squares is it from the sandpit, straight across to the swings?
items.e: Count each move to the right: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. That is 5 squares. Do not count the sandpit square.

items.q: Which steps take you from the gate to the bubblers?
items.e: From the gate, count the squares across, then the squares up or down: 1 square right, then 3 squares up. Count the moves, not the square you start on.

items.q: Ruby walks from the climbing frame straight to the swings. Which way does she go on the map?
items.e: The swings are in the same row as the climbing frame, on the right side. So she goes right.

items.q: Start at the bike racks. Go 1 square up, then 1 square left. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the bike racks. Go 1 square up, then 1 square left. You reach the garden. Do not count the square you start on.

items.q: Isla is at the gate. She walks straight to the sandpit. Which way does she go on the map?
items.e: The sandpit is in the same column as the gate, nearer the top of the map. So she goes up.

items.q: Which steps take you from the library to the bench?
items.e: From the library, count the squares across, then the squares up or down: 4 squares left, then 3 squares down. Count the moves, not the square you start on.

items.q: How many squares is it from the bike racks, straight up to the library?
items.e: Count each move up: 1, 2, 3, 4. That is 4 squares. If you count the bike racks square too, you get 5, which is too many.

items.q: Follow the dashed path from the red dot to the star. Which steps does it show?
items.e: Count the squares along the path from the dot: 4 squares left, then 1 square up. Do not count the dot’s own square.

items.q: Start at the library. Go 2 squares down. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the library. Go 2 squares down. You reach the swings. Do not count the square you start on.

items.q: Which steps take you from the sandpit to the garden?
items.e: From the sandpit, count the squares across, then the squares up or down: 4 squares right, then 1 square down. Count the moves, not the square you start on.

items.q: Start at the gate. Go 2 squares up. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the gate. Go 2 squares up. You reach the sandpit. Do not count the square you start on.

items.q: Start at the garden. Go 4 squares left, then 1 square down. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the garden. Go 4 squares left, then 1 square down. You reach the gate. Do not count the square you start on.

items.q: Start at the sports shed. Go 3 squares up, then 2 squares right. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the sports shed. Go 3 squares up, then 2 squares right. You reach the gum tree. Do not count the square you start on.

items.q: Start at the toilets. Go 3 squares down, then 2 squares left. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the toilets. Go 3 squares down, then 2 squares left. You reach the bench. Do not count the square you start on.

items.q: Start at the swings. Go 4 squares left, then 1 square up. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the swings. Go 4 squares left, then 1 square up. You reach the bubblers. Do not count the square you start on.

items.q: Follow the dashed path from the red dot to the flag. Which steps does it show?
items.e: Count the squares along the path from the dot: 2 squares up, then 3 squares right. Do not count the dot’s own square.

items.q: Follow the dashed path from the red dot to the house. Which steps does it show?
items.e: Count the squares along the path from the dot: 3 squares right, then 2 squares down. Do not count the dot’s own square.

items.q: Start at the sandpit. Go 1 square down, then 1 square right. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the sandpit. Go 1 square down, then 1 square right. You reach the bench. Do not count the square you start on.

sets.title: Count the squares: which path is shorter?

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path B?
items.e: Count each move along path B from the house: 4 + 4. That is 8 squares. Do not count the house square.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path A?
items.e: Count each move along path A from the house: 4 + 3. That is 7 squares. Do not count the house square.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. Which path is shorter, and by how much?
items.e: Path A is 8 squares. Path B is 8 squares. They are the same length, even though one has more turns.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. Which path is shorter, and by how much?
items.e: Path A is 10 squares. Path B is 8 squares. 8 is less than 10, so path B is shorter. 10 − 8 = 2.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path B?
items.e: Count each move along path B from the house: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2. That is 7 squares. Do not count the house square.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path B?
items.e: Count each move along path B from the house: 1 + 6 + 1. That is 8 squares. Do not count the house square.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path B?
items.e: Count each move along path B from the house: 1 + 4 + 5. That is 10 squares. Do not count the house square.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path A?
items.e: Count each move along path A from the house: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2. That is 8 squares. Do not count the house square.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. Which path is shorter, and by how much?
items.e: Path A is 7 squares. Path B is 7 squares. They are the same length, even though one has more turns.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. Which path is shorter, and by how much?
items.e: Path A is 8 squares. Path B is 10 squares. 8 is less than 10, so path A is shorter. 10 − 8 = 2.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. Which path is shorter, and by how much?
items.e: Path A is 10 squares. Path B is 8 squares. 8 is less than 10, so path B is shorter. 10 − 8 = 2.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path B?
items.e: Count each move along path B from the house: 5 + 3 + 1. That is 9 squares. Do not count the house square.

items.q: What is the shortest path from the house to the flag? How many squares long is it?
items.e: Go straight across and straight up, with no going back: 5 across + 3 up = 8 squares.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path A?
items.e: Count each move along path A from the house: 4 + 5 + 1. That is 10 squares. Do not count the house square.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path A?
items.e: Count each move along path A from the house: 2 + 6 + 2. That is 10 squares. Do not count the house square.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. Which path is shorter, and by how much?
items.e: Path A is 8 squares. Path B is 12 squares. 8 is less than 12, so path A is shorter. 12 − 8 = 4.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path A?
items.e: Count each move along path A from the house: 3 + 4. That is 7 squares. Do not count the house square.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path A?
items.e: Count each move along path A from the house: 5 + 3. That is 8 squares. Do not count the house square.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. Which path is shorter, and by how much?
items.e: Path A is 7 squares. Path B is 9 squares. 7 is less than 9, so path A is shorter. 9 − 7 = 2.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path B?
items.e: Count each move along path B from the house: 5 + 3. That is 8 squares. Do not count the house square.

sets.title: Bird’s-eye views and real-life map problems

items.q: Which picture shows the table with 4 chairs from above (a bird’s-eye view)?
items.e: A bird’s-eye view shows something from above, like a bird flying over it. Picture B shows the table with 4 chairs from above. Picture A shows it from the side.

items.q: The class goes to the park on an excursion. Jack stands at the red dot. He faces right, towards the pond. Where is the picnic table for him?
items.e: Jack faces right (towards the pond). When you face right on the page, your right hand points down the page. Turn the map so Jack faces up to check. The picnic table is on his right.

items.q: The class goes to the park on an excursion. Chloe cooks sausages at the BBQ. Then she walks 3 squares right and 1 square down. Where is she?
items.e: From the BBQ go right 3 squares, then down 1 square. That is the sandpit. Counting the BBQ square as 1 stops you at the pond.

items.q: The class goes to the park on an excursion. Mia stands at the red dot. She faces up the page, towards the gum tree. Where is the BBQ for her?
items.e: Mia faces up the page (towards the gum tree). She faces the same way as you, so her left and right are the same as the page. The BBQ is on her left.

items.q: Which picture shows the tree from above (a bird’s-eye view)?
items.e: A bird’s-eye view shows something from above, like a bird flying over it. Picture C shows the tree from above. Picture A shows it from the side.

items.q: The class goes to the park on an excursion. Ava stands at the red dot. She faces left, towards the BBQ. Where is the gum tree for her?
items.e: Ava faces left (towards the BBQ). When you face left on the page, your right hand points up the page. Turn the map so Ava faces up to check. The gum tree is on her right.

items.q: The class goes to the park on an excursion. Harper goes from the gate to the swings: 3 right, then 2 up. Sienna goes 2 up, then 3 right. Who walks further?
items.e: Harper walks 3 + 2 = 5 squares. Sienna walks 2 + 3 = 5 squares. They walk the same: 5 squares each.

items.q: The class goes to the park on an excursion. Matilda walks 3 squares right from the BBQ, then 3 squares left. Where is she now?
items.e: 3 right, then 3 left takes her back to where she started: the BBQ.

items.q: Ruby draws a plan of her bedroom. The desk is on the left of the bed. The door is below the desk. Which plan is right?
items.e: Left is the left side of the page. Below means just under. The desk is just left of the bed and the door is just under the desk. That is plan A.

items.q: The class goes to the park on an excursion. Mei stands at the red dot. She faces down the page, towards the picnic table. Where is the pond for her?
items.e: Mei faces down the page (towards the picnic table). She faces you, so her left and right are swapped. Turn the map upside down to check. The pond is on her left.

items.q: Which picture shows the car from above (a bird’s-eye view)?
items.e: A bird’s-eye view shows something from above, like a bird flying over it. Picture D shows the car from above. Picture A shows it from the side.

items.q: This is a bird’s-eye view. What is it?
items.e: A round shape with a handle on one side. It is a cup of hot chocolate seen from above.

items.q: The class goes to the park on an excursion. Liam is at the slide. Next he wants a go on the swings. Which steps take him there?
items.e: The swings are 1 square right of the slide and 1 square down. Mixing up left and right, or up and down, sends him the wrong way.

items.q: Oliver draws a plan of his backyard. The tree is above the bench. The ball is on the right of the bench. Which plan is right?
items.e: Above means just over it, towards the top of the page. Right is the right side of the page. The tree is over the bench and the ball is just right of it. That is plan A.

items.q: The class goes to the park on an excursion. Each square on the map is 10 big steps. Lachlan walks from the gate straight to the shelter. How many big steps is that?
items.e: The shelter is 2 squares right of the gate. 2 squares is 10 + 10 = 20 big steps. Counting the gate square too gives 30, which is too many.

items.q: The class goes to the park on an excursion. Which of these is closest to the gate?
items.e: Count the squares from the gate. The picnic table is only 2 squares away (1 left and 1 up). The others are further away.

items.q: This is a bird’s-eye view. What is it?
items.e: You can see a pillow at one end and a blanket. It is a bed seen from above.

items.q: The class goes to the park on an excursion. Noah stands at the red dot. He faces down the page, towards the picnic table. Where is the BBQ for him?
items.e: Noah faces down the page (towards the picnic table). He faces you, so his left and right are swapped. Turn the map upside down to check. The BBQ is on his right.

items.q: The class goes to the park on an excursion. Aarav walks from the gate 2 squares up. What does he reach?
items.e: From the gate, count the moves up: 1 (an empty square), 2 (the pond). Do not count the gate square.

items.q: The class goes to the park on an excursion. Oliver leaves the toilets. He goes 2 squares down, then 2 squares right. What does he reach?
items.e: From the toilets go down 2 squares to the BBQ, then right 2 squares to the pond. Counting the start square each time stops you at the gum tree.
